newsitem.title: CANADA: ID Biomed hopes to clinch test alliance.
newsitem.headline: ID Biomed hopes to clinch test alliance.

text.p: Seeking to reassure impatient investors, ID Biomedical Corp told stockholders on Friday it hopes finally to secure an alliance with a major pharmaceutical company on its DNA-based disease testing technology this year.

The biotechnology company had aimed to strike such an accord in the fiscal year ended in March but failed to do so. Several shareholders at the annual meeting expressed concern about the delay and complained about a halving in ID's share price over the past year to around C$4.75.
Yet Chief Executive Frank Holler said he was confident a deal would be reached based on ID's strong progress in developing its cycling probe technology (CPT).

"We've been in discussions for several years with a number of different parties...I think it's just a matter of time before alliances are completed. I know it's frustrating for shareholders," he said after facing pointed questioning.
"I think we are on the verge of having those alliances."

ID believes CPT offers a fast, simple and inexpensive platform for testing gene sequences as a way of identifying diseases. Its first two products are tests for the MRSA and VRE "superbugs," which use CPT to detect genes responsible for antibiotic resistance.

In an interview after the meeting, Holler said ID was in discussions with more than 12 potential partners for broad collaboration deals that would include licensing and co-development of CPT and vaccines.
Holler said one of the companies ID had been negotiating with on CPT was Boehringer Mannheim Group -- which was recently acquired by Switzerland's Roche Holding Ltd as part of a US$11 billion deal.

Holler said ID had shown in the past year that CPT could be commercially applied, an achievement that should give major companies the confidence they need to enter an alliance. ID anticipates its MRSA test will begin commercial sales early in 1998.

The company has about C$11.1 million in working capital, enough to fund 22 months of operations, Holler said. It is looking at opportunities for raising capital but is not under immediate pressure to do so.

ID already has an alliance with the Pasteur Meriuex Connaught unit of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer Inc on a vaccine for tuberculosis. They plan to finalize formulation of the vaccine before the end of this fiscal year.

The company plans to begin clinical trials around the end of the year on a vaccine against Group A streptococcus and is beginning work on developing a vaccine against the strain of e. coli bacteria that causes potentially deadlly "hamburger disease."
Holler said ID was negotiating to license other vaccines and hoped to acquire at least one more by the end of this fiscal year.

Responding to shareholder concerns about ID's stock fall, Holler said that partly reflected general market trends for biotechnology issues. He also said it was common among biotech firms for their stock performance not to keep pace with research developments.
"I hope you get the sense we share your disappointment. (Market activity) is absolutely not reflective of what is going on within the company," said Chairman John Smith.
